A.explanation: Both dossiers share the federal regime: a binary-sex executive order, passport/visa gender restrictions now in force, a consular cable ordering refusal where documents cast doubt on sex with possible lifetime fraud ineligibility, facility exclusion mapped across 21 states (4 with criminal provisions, one documented arrest), documented abuse in immigration custody, a federal conversion-therapy-style prison policy, and hostile official framing. A's territory adds only a gender-identity anti-discrimination statute and settled marriage law, with no recorded enforcement, and cannot alter entry, documents or federal custody. Public opinion backs birth-sex documents (66%). No execution or routine imprisonment risk; universal document and facility exposure plus a severe custody tail keeps A in Elevated Risk.

entry_documents.exposure: Jan 2025 order bars gender self-selection on passports/visas; Nov 2025 ruling lets marker restrictions take effect; 24 Feb 2025 cable directs refusal where documents/records cast reasonable doubt on sex, and asks officers to consider lifetime fraud ineligibility; 8+ governments issued trans travel advisories; travellers report passports blocked or seized.
entry_documents.protection: Existing X-marker passports valid to expiry; civil-liberties suit pending; fraud finding requires all four elements, has limited waivers and is never automatic; legal-aid FAQ advises on document strategy.
entry_documents.interaction: The territory's human-rights statute does not reach entry screening, visa adjudication or federal document rules; local anti-discrimination cannot cure a refused visa or a blocked passport.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Immigration custody: trans men report forced labour, beatings, solitary confinement and severe sexual abuse. Federal corrections bureau adopted a 2026 conversion-therapy-style policy (hair cut short, hormones removed, psychiatric drugs). One documented restroom arrest: handcuffed, 24 hours held in a men's ward.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: National hate-crime statute covers gender identity; several January 2025 orders enjoined; legal-aid FAQ; formal judicial review exists.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Detention follows discovery at entry or in a facility encounter; the territory's protections do not govern federal custody or federal prison policy.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Federal order bars trans people from government-funded single-sex facilities; mapping (Nov 2026) shows 21 state/provinces with bans (9 covering all government buildings), 4 with criminal provisions, 6 extending into some private settings; one documented arrest under such a law.
federal_state_facilities.protection: 29 state/provinces plus the capital district have no mapped ban; the territory has no documented ban and its human-rights statute prohibits gender-identity discrimination.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: The territory statute cannot override the federal facility order or another state's law; actual exposure depends on which buildings the itinerary enters.

care_services.exposure: Oct 2025 proposed federal rule would bar public-insurance reimbursement for under-18 trans care; DOJ subpoenaed 20+ hospitals for under-19 patient records; LGBTQ youth crisis-line services shut down; 27 states bar youth gender-affirming care.
care_services.protection: No territory-specific care restriction documented; adult care not nationally banned; several measures are proposed or enjoined; litigation pending.
care_services.interaction: Federal funding and subpoena powers reach clinics inside the territory; the local statute secures no care entitlement.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Official framing: 'chemical and surgical mutilation' order, directive to investigate schools and prosecute those facilitating social transition, 'radical gender ideology' in a Dec 2025 reward memo, May 2026 counterterrorism strategy prioritising 'radically pro-transgender' groups; 66% poll backs birth-sex document rules.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: The memo states the phrase is never the reward criterion; the strategy says counterterrorism powers will not target mere disagreement; courts enjoined several orders; national employment and hate-crime protections remain.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Framing raises the probability of being noticed and the severity of police encounters even where no charge lies.

minors_guardians.exposure: Jan 29 2025 order directs law enforcement to investigate schools and criminally prosecute those facilitating a trans minor's social transition, including names/pronouns; 27 states bar youth care plus a proposed federal insurance rule; hospital-record subpoenas expose minors' data.
minors_guardians.protection: Territory's 2017 chief-legal-officer interpretation extends anti-discrimination law to transgender students; marriage and adoption settled; measures contested in court.
minors_guardians.interaction: A travelling guardian cannot rely on that interpretation against federal charges, federal funding rules or a refused prescription.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: No territory violence data recorded. Nationally: one documented restroom arrest with trespass charge; 4 state/provinces flagged 'Do Not Travel' for trans people (July 2026); criminal-facility provisions in 4 states; poll hostility toward birth-sex document rules.
street_violence_police_response.protection: Federal hate-crime statute covers gender identity; 23 state/provinces cover gender identity in bias statutes; territory statute offers a service-refusal remedy.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Territory recourse is untested (no enforcement records) and does not reach street violence or federal policing.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: July 2026 assessment says the 2026 legislative season kept degrading trans rights; no territory enforcement actions or trans-violence data recorded; several federal measures' status shifts with ongoing litigation.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Civil-liberties suit pending, multiple injunctions, a running legal-aid FAQ, an in-force territory human-rights statute, marriage equality settled.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Remedy quality inside the territory is unproven while the federal exposure layer is largely fixed and traveller-facing.

anchor_checks.comparison: Higher than 0.25-C: A has no cross-dressing offence in administrative buildings and only one documented restroom arrest, versus routine raids, fines and frequent birth-sex prison assault there. Both share birth-sex custody placement and slow remedies, which keeps A only a step above rather than a tier.

Similar entry exposure: Vellandra's unpublished exclusion register maps onto the consular cable's refusal-on-discrepancy rule with thin appeal and foreign advisories. A sits slightly above because refusals are individualised, litigation is live, and existing X passports remain valid, though the lifetime fraud finding is harsher than exclusion alone.

Below 0.55-B: Kestrel Isles' secondary screening ends in administrative return with written reasons and an appeal desk. A's discrepancy can trigger permanent fraud ineligibility, plus mapped facility bans with criminal provisions and documented abuse in immigration custody — heavier severity at comparable or higher probability.

Well below 0.75-C: Meridia trains officers for respectful inspection, recognises trans passports, and offers tribunal compensation for detention. A has no such inspection regime, an active refusal-on-discrepancy instruction, and state-level facility exclusion with one arrest — the opposite of a protective border posture.

A.synthesis: The operative regime is the federal layer plus a thin local shield. Entry is where discovery concentrates: a discrepancy between documents and presentation can produce refusal and, under the fraud ground, lasting ineligibility — hence eight foreign advisories. Downstream, government-funded single-sex facilities are closed to trans people by federal order and by 21 state bans, four criminalising; airports add invasive screening. Detention converts outing into documented harm (immigration abuse, federal birth-sex prison policy with hormone withdrawal). The territory's human-rights statute mitigates ordinary service refusals locally but has no recorded enforcement and cannot reach borders, federal buildings or custody. Courts remain partly working — several orders enjoined, litigation active — which holds A above the 0.35 tier while universal document and facility exposure keeps it in Elevated Risk.

B.explanation: The combined regime is the same federal layer — binary-sex order, visa cable triggering refusal and possible lifetime fraud ineligibility on sex discrepancy, government-facility exclusion, documented immigration-detention abuse and federal birth-sex prison policy — plus a state adding hostile layers of its own: a 2023 executive order ending recognition of trans people, surgery-based document rules, an under-19 care ban upheld 6-1, a total sports ban, no statewide gender-identity discrimination or hate-crime coverage, and a documented prison assault on a trans woman placed by birth sex whose claims the courts dismissed. For an outed adult, entry and facility exposure dominate; for a travelling family, care denial and outing compound. No execution or likely imprisonment, but state-endorsed exclusion with failed remedies holds B in High Risk.

entry_documents.exposure: Federal: Feb 2025 order bars gender self-selection on passports/visas; Nov 2025 ruling lets marker restrictions stand; consular cable orders refusal where documents cast doubt on sex, with possible lifetime fraud ineligibility. State: 2023 executive order directs all agencies to binary biological sex definitions.
entry_documents.protection: Existing X-marker passports valid to expiry; suit pending; fraud finding needs four elements with limited waivers. The state's surgery-affidavit rules govern only locally issued IDs, not a foreign passport.
entry_documents.interaction: Entry itself is federal; the state's binary-definition order shapes any state-office encounter (licensing, courts, state buildings) the visitor may have after arrival.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Federal: abuse of trans men in immigration custody (forced labour, beatings, solitary, sexual abuse) and a 2026 federal conversion-therapy-style prison policy. State: trans woman housed by birth sex among men, cellled with a convicted male sex offender who assaulted her; all claims (failure to treat, protect, provide surgery) dismissed 10 Aug 2022; federal transfer-to-identity placement rescinded 2018.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Federal hate-crime statute covers gender identity; suits are filable though this one failed; consular/judicial review exists federally.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: A border or facility encounter can move the visitor from federal screening into birth-sex placement, where the state's courts have already endorsed the practice with no effective remedy.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Federal order excludes trans people from government-funded single-sex facilities; mapping shows 21 state/provinces with bans. The state's 2023 order backs single-sex bathrooms and changing rooms and directs agencies to biological definitions; no facility-use enforcement provision is recorded (uncertain).
federal_state_facilities.protection: One city has barred gender-identity discrimination in employment and public accommodations since 2012; national employment (2020) and housing (2021) rules apply; a second city's 2022 ordinance was repealed by petition.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: The state order aligns with and reinforces the federal facility regime; the absence of a statewide gender-identity statute leaves any exclusion without local recourse.

care_services.exposure: State bars gender-affirming care for under-19s (passed 33-15, signed immediately 2023, upheld 6-1 July 2024): a trans visitor under 19, or a guardian seeking care for a minor in their care, is refused. Federal Oct 2025 proposed rule would bar under-18 public-insurance reimbursement; DOJ subpoenaed under-19 hospital records.
care_services.protection: Adult care not barred by the state; emergency care not documented as denied; several federal measures enjoined or merely proposed.
care_services.interaction: A travelling family meets both layers at once, and the state's own high court has constitutionalised the bar.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: 2023 order 'ends state recognition of transgender people' and imposes biological definitions on agencies; the 1997 state hate-crime law omits gender identity; federal memo and May 2026 strategy use 'radical gender ideology' and 'radically pro-transgender' framing; 66% poll backs birth-sex document rules.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Federal hate-crime statute covers gender identity; 2020 employment and 2021 housing enforcement apply; federal courts have enjoined several orders; 2016 state high court upheld the hate-crime law in a perceived-association case.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Official state threat-framing reduces the likelihood that police treat a trans complaint as genuine, weakening federal protections in practice.

minors_guardians.exposure: Under-19 care ban; June 2025 law barring trans athletes from any sports (two-thirds majority); school athletics require HRT/surgery evidence; a minor's name change requires two weeks' newspaper publication — compelled outing. Federal order threatens prosecution over facilitating social transition.
minors_guardians.protection: Marriage and adoption recognition settled; national employment protections; one city's ordinance and the college system's 2021 policy cover gender identity.
minors_guardians.interaction: A parent travelling with a trans minor risks care denial, publication-based outing and state inquiry, overlaid by federal prosecution exposure.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: No state-level trans violence statistics recorded; the documented custody sexual assault with dismissed claims; one city's gender-identity ordinance repealed by petition in June 2022 — a social-hostility signal; state hate-crime law does not name gender identity.
street_violence_police_response.protection: Federal hate-crime prosecution available; national bias-incident statistics are collected; police cannot refuse a report entirely given federal coverage.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Absence of counts is not safety; state silence plus dismissed claims plausibly depresses reporting and response quality.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: The assaulted prisoner's failure-to-protect, treatment and surgery claims were all dismissed — institutional remedy failed where the state's own policy operates; no statewide gender-identity anti-discrimination or hate-crime statute; post-2023 marker practice unresolved; several federal provisions enjoined or pending.
remedies_unknowns.protection: National employment, housing and hate-crime machinery; one city's ordinances; a legal-aid FAQ; ongoing federal litigation producing injunctions.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Recourse exists federally but not against the state's own hostile rule, which its courts endorsed rather than checked.

anchor_checks.comparison: Well above 0.15-B: no months-long border detention, withheld medical care, deferred habeas or credible capital exposure; entry refusals are administrative and courts function. B nevertheless shares 0.15-B's birth-sex custody harm in documented form, which prevents a much higher score.

Slightly below 0.35-A: entry is comparably hostile (cable refusal plus lifetime fraud ineligibility, no reliable appeal), but B adds layers Vellandra lacks — a state order ending recognition, an under-19 care ban upheld by its own high court, and a prison assault its courts dismissed.

Below 0.45-B: Aldermere's school-registry and emergency-only care limits resemble B's under-19 care ban, but B compounds that with birth-sex prison placement its judiciary upheld, surgery-based document rules, a total sports ban, and no statewide gender-identity discrimination or hate-crime coverage — worse recourse and more punitive statutes.

Far below 0.75-C: Meridia trains officers for respectful inspection and offers tribunal compensation for detention. B's state layer moves the opposite direction — executive-order non-recognition, care denial upheld 6-1, and judicial dismissal of a trans prisoner's assault claims.

B.synthesis: B is the shared federal exposure plus an additive hostile state layer. The federal regime already fixes discovery risk at the border (refusal on sex discrepancy, possible lifetime fraud ineligibility), closes government-funded single-sex facilities, and produces documented abuse in immigration and federal custody. The state then reinforces every one of those points: its 2023 order directs agencies to binary definitions and 'ends recognition'; its courts upheld an under-19 care ban and dismissed the claims of a trans woman assaulted after birth-sex placement; its hate-crime and anti-discrimination laws omit gender identity. For families, care denial and publication-based outing compound federal school-prosecution risk. Federal injunctions and hate-crime coverage are real but do not reach the state's own operative practices — hence a step below A, inside High Risk.
